title: Nancy Mace introduces School Freedom Act and addresses failed censure attempts
text:
← Back to the wire
Nancy Mace introduces School Freedom Act and addresses failed censure attempts
Rep. Nancy Mace detailed new education legislation and recounted failed congressional censure votes against colleagues Ilhan Omar and Cory Mills on October 15, 2026.
Rep. Nancy Mace, U.S. Congresswoman representing South Carolina’s 1st district since 2021, announced the introduction of the School Freedom Act and commented on recent congressional censure efforts in a series of posts on October 15, 2026.
In her first post at 17:30 UTC, Mace wrote: "INTRODUCING: The School Freedom Act to send federal K-12 money directly to parents through a School Freedom Account. Federal K-12 programs wind down by June 30, 2027. In their place, every eligible student gets a School Freedom Account funded with those federal dollars. Public".
Later that day at 19:30 UTC, she addressed recent censure attempts in Congress: "We tried to censure Ilhan Omar and Cory Mills. Both times, Congress protected its own. In September 2025, we tried to censure Omar and strip her of her committee assignments for her vile comments mocking the assassination of Charlie Kirk. The House voted 214-213 to table it,".
At 20:30 UTC, Mace posted a follow-up referencing Rep. Ilhan Omar, "The typo is actually a nod to Congresswoman Omar.".
Mace has served in the U.S. Congress since replacing Joe Cunningham in 2021 and previously held office in the South Carolina House of Representatives from 2018 to 2020. She was born in Fort Bragg, North Carolina in 1977 and currently resides in Charleston. Mace graduated from The Citadel with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1999.
